views.label: Confining flow

start.text: the surface runs on to the singularity $r = 0$, nearing the light cone

end.text: the surface runs on toward the boundary, $r \to \infty$

views.settings: $L = 1$, the strip $0 \le x_1 < 2\pi L$ rolled up, every length measured with $dX^2 + dY^2 - dZ^2$.
stops: Every circle grows faster than the distance out to it, so no surface of revolution in Euclidean space has this geometry; one in Minkowski space does.
caption: The surface of $r$ and $x_1$ at $t = 0$ of the confining flow in Minkowski space, from $r = L/20$ near the singularity out toward the boundary, close to a light cone throughout.

views.label: Disc of branes

start.text: the singularity $v = 0$, where the circles shrink to a point

end.text: the surface runs on toward the boundary, $v \to 1$

views.settings: $L = 1$, $\ell = 3L/2$, the strip $0 \le x_1 < 2\pi L$ rolled up, every length measured with $dX^2 + dY^2 - dZ^2$.
stops: Every circle grows faster than the distance out to it, so no surface of revolution in Euclidean space has this geometry; one in Minkowski space does.
caption: The surface of $v$ and $x_1$ at $t = 0$ of the disc of branes ($\ell = 3L/2$) in Minkowski space, level at the singularity $v = 0$ on its axis and rising toward the boundary.
